z1r.about: One whole number written in the alphabet, most significant digit first. The fields are read in position order, the first least significant: each field's value is the number modulo its radix, and the number is then divided by the radix (whole division).

rules.character_outside_alphabet: refused; an alphabet_aliases character reads as its digit
rules.leading_zeros: ignored: '0' is the zero digit, so they change nothing
rules.option_digit_at_or_above_value_count: read as the field's last value (len(values) - 1)

zora.about: '<version>.<payload>': a decimal version, a dot, then one whole number in the alphabet. The fields whose added_in_version is at most the string's version are read in position order, the first least significant, as in the Z1R string. A field added after the string's version is at its default.

rules.character_outside_alphabet: refused; an alphabet_aliases character reads as its digit
rules.number_left_after_the_last_field: refused (a mistyped string never turns into other flags)
rules.retired_field: read and ignored: its place stays, so every older string still decodes
rules.canonical_spelling: empty when every field is at its default; otherwise the lowest version holding every field away from its default, then the payload without leading zeros

tracker_hints.about: What a player can know at the start from the flags alone: items pinned to a place, and start items. A condition list matches when any of its conditions does; a condition matches when every field it names (a Z1R key or a ZORA key) holds one of the listed values. Nothing here depends on the seed: where a seed's draw decides, the hint is unknown.

pins.about: A pin value names the item at its place when the pins apply (applies_when); when unknown_when matches it may or may not be there; otherwise the pins do nothing and the place's item is not known from the flags. A level 9 pin names the item at the first (or second) of level 9's item places; it does nothing if level 9 has no such place.

start_items.about: A start item's field at On gives the item at the start when the limit keeps every chosen item: its limit is null, or the count of start-item fields that are not Off is at most the limit. Otherwise, and for a field at Random, the item is unknown (the seed draws it).

modifiers.about: Each pair's two items trade places. A pair is not swapped when the seed starts with either of its items: when one of its start_item_fields is not Off, the pair's items are swapped only if both are certainly not start items, kept as they are if one certainly is, and unknown otherwise.
The boomerangs' items are the boots (the seed format's names).
Wood Sword Only and Swordless: the White Sword item is still named so, but taking it adds two bombs to the bomb capacity instead of giving a sword.

Each item of an upgrade line found in the world gives the next item of that line the player lacks, whichever item of the line it is named. Start items are not changed: a start item is the item itself. Each line's items are listed lowest first.

file_name.about: The page names each seed's files <prefix>-<version>-<Z1R flag string>-<ZORA flag string>-<seed>, then the music ending when the seed has randomized music, then the file's extension. The page writes the alphabet's '!' as its alias '_' (alphabet_aliases), so each flag part is a flag string as it stands: decode it as it is. An empty ZORA string (every ZORA field at its default) leaves '--'. Neither flag string holds '-', so a name also reads from the right: past any music ending, the seed, the ZORA string, the Z1R string, then the version, which may hold '-'.

parts.about: The ZORA version the page shows, its spaces as '-' and parentheses dropped: '2.0.1' on the regular channel. On the test channel the build's short commit follows it and '-test' ends it: '2.0.1-a1b2c3d-test'. A version is not a flag; ZoraTracker's ZoraVersion and the spec's zora_version are the release version without these.
The ZORA flag string; empty when every ZORA field is at its default.
'-music' when the seed has randomized music (Music: Random, a player setting in neither flag string); absent otherwise.

batch_zip.about: Several seeds at once: a .zip named for the first seed's stem, then '-' and the last seed, then the music ending. It holds each seed's files under the names above; a batch saved to a folder writes the same names.

duplicate_suffix.about: A browser that saves a name twice adds a number before the extension: ' (1)' (Chrome, Edge) or '(1)' (Firefox). Remove it before matching.

tolerate.renamed: A name that does not match the pattern is not the page's: read nothing from it, and ask for the flag strings to be pasted instead.
tolerate.before_2_0_1: ZORA before 2.0.1 named files zora-seed-<seed>.nes (with '-encoded' or '-music' before the extension) and batches zora-seeds-<first>-<last>.zip: those names hold the seed only, no version or flags, and match neither pattern.
tolerate.archipelago: Archipelago names its files itself (AP_<multiworld seed>_P<player>_<player name>, .apzora for the patch and .nes for the ROM it makes): they hold no ZORA flags, and match neither pattern.
